# Story 11 — Knowledge Base & Customer Portal (Story: 11)

## Prerequisites

- Stories 01–10 completed and merged into `main` (staff auth/RBAC, audit logging, Customer/Ticket CRUD, notes/attachments/tasks/quick-replies, SLA/escalation/notifications, App Shell, i18n/RTL).
- Reuses Story 03/04's JWT/RBAC pattern (`JwtTokenService`, `[Authorize]`, `[Authorize(Roles=...)]`), Story 05's `AuditLogger`/`AuditLog`, Story 07/08's `Ticket` entity as-is, Story 09's `TicketNote` history read pattern and `QuickReplyTemplate` staff-CRUD-page precedent, Story 10's `NotificationsController` 404-not-403 authorization convention.
- No coordination needed with external owners — all touched surfaces are inside this repo.

---

## Story Goal

Introduce Knowledge Base authoring/browsing and a customer-facing Portal on top of the existing CRM, while adding a **second identity kind** (`type=customer`) alongside the existing staff (`type=staff`) identity, using a **single** JWT bearer scheme and ASP.NET Core **claim-based authorization policies** to keep the two identities strictly separated.

User-visible outcomes:

1. Staff (Admin **or** Agent) can create/edit/delete/list/search Knowledge Base articles from a new staff page.
2. A customer can register + log in to a customer portal (distinct login screen, distinct shell), receiving a JWT with a `type=customer` claim.
3. A customer can submit new tickets (owned by themselves, server-resolved from the token), list and view **only** their own tickets with history/notes, and submit feedback on tickets whose `Status == "Closed"`.
4. A customer can browse and keyword-search the Knowledge Base (read-only).
5. Every existing staff-only endpoint rejects a customer token; every new customer-only endpoint rejects a staff token; the KB list/search endpoint accepts both; KB write endpoints accept only staff.

**Not in scope:** anonymous ticket submission, a second auth scheme, a separate `CustomerAccount` entity, password reset, customer profile self-editing, KB categories/tags/attachments/versioning, search on staff-side Tickets/Customers, reporting/aggregation over feedback, AI features. See intake "Out of scope".

## Product rules (from story)

- **Decision 1 — Customer identity is `Customer` + nullable `PasswordHash`.** No `CustomerAccount` entity.
- **Decision 2 — Single JWT bearer scheme + `type` claim + ASP.NET Core policies.** No second auth scheme.
- **Decision 3 — Admin *and* Agent may CRUD KB articles.** No admin-only restriction.
- **Decision 4 — Feedback allowed only when `Ticket.Status == "Closed"` (exact match).** Server-enforced.
- **Decision 5 — Portal ticket submission requires authenticated customer.** No anonymous path.

These decisions are approved and **must not be re-litigated** during implementation. Deviating requires explicit intake amendment.

### 2 — Generalize `JwtTokenService`

**File: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Auth/JwtTokenService.cs`**

Change the signature to be identity-kind-agnostic:

```csharp
public string IssueToken(
    Guid subjectId,
    string email,
    string displayName,
    string identityType,      // "staff" | "customer"
    IEnumerable<string> roles, // empty for customers
    out DateTime expiresAtUtc);
```

Emit these claims:

- `sub` = `subjectId.ToString()`
- `email` = `email`
- `name` = `displayName`
- **`type` = `identityType`** (new — this is the claim policies key off)
- one `ClaimTypes.Role` per `roles` entry (empty for customers)

Keep the existing signing key, issuer, audience, and lifetime source unchanged.

Add a thin overload `IssueToken(User user, IEnumerable<string> roles, out DateTime expiresAtUtc)` that forwards to the new signature with `identityType = "staff"`, so `AuthController.cs` at line 67 continues to compile without change.

Do **not** create a parallel `JwtTokenService` for customers.

### 3 — Authorization policies + DI

**File: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Program.cs`**

3.1. Register the customer password hasher next to the existing `PasswordHasher<User>` registration:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddScoped<PasswordHasher<Customer>>();
```

3.2. Add two authorization policies:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddAuthorization(options =>
{
    options.AddPolicy("RequireStaff",
        p => p.RequireAuthenticatedUser().RequireClaim("type", "staff"));
    options.AddPolicy("RequireCustomer",
        p => p.RequireAuthenticatedUser().RequireClaim("type", "customer"));
});
```

3.3. If a default policy is currently configured, leave it as-is; the two policies above are applied per-controller/action.

3.4. Verify by inspection that `AdminController` (audit log endpoint) is `[Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]`; upgrade to `[Authorize(Policy = "RequireStaff", Roles = "Admin")]` so a customer token with a forged `role=Admin` claim (or any customer token) is rejected before role check.

3.5. Sweep **every** existing controller and upgrade the class-level or action-level `[Authorize]` to include the staff policy:
   - `TicketsController.cs`
   - `CustomersController.cs`
   - `NotificationsController.cs`
   - `AdminController.cs`
   - `QuickRepliesController.cs`
   - The audit-log endpoint (wherever it lives — see AdminController.cs)
   - Any other `[Authorize]`-decorated controller found by the grep in Context item 14

For each, change the attribute from `[Authorize]` (or `[Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]`) to `[Authorize(Policy = "RequireStaff")]` (or `[Authorize(Policy = "RequireStaff", Roles = "Admin")]`). Do **not** change `[AllowAnonymous]` on `HealthController` or on staff `POST /api/auth/login`.

### 4 — Customer login / register

**File: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Controllers/AuthController.cs`** (add sibling actions) **or new `PortalAuthController.cs`** — either is acceptable; pick the sibling-actions form to minimize surface. Route them under `POST /api/portal/auth/register` and `POST /api/portal/auth/login`, both `[AllowAnonymous]`.

DTOs — new file **`backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Controllers/PortalAuthDtos.cs`**:

```csharp
public record CustomerRegisterRequest(string FullName, string Email, string? Phone, string Password);
public record CustomerLoginRequest(string Email, string Password);
public record CustomerLoginResponse(string Token, DateTime ExpiresAtUtc, Guid CustomerId, string Email, string FullName);
```

Rules:

- **Register:** `Email` unique (409 on collision); `Password` min length 8 (match staff rule if different); hash with `PasswordHasher<Customer>`; if a `Customer` row with this email already exists but has `PasswordHash == null`, allow the register call to **set** the password on the existing row (this preserves customer records staff created in Stories 06–10). Audit-log the register event.
- **Login:** look up by `Email` (case-insensitive); reject 401 if row missing, `PasswordHash == null`, or verification fails. Issue token with `identityType = "customer"`, `roles = Array.Empty<string>()`, `subjectId = customer.Id`. Audit-log the login event.
- **Both** actions are `[AllowAnonymous]`. All other new portal actions below are `[Authorize(Policy = "RequireCustomer")]`.

```csharp
private Guid GetActorCustomerId()
{
    var raw = User.FindFirst("sub")?.Value
        ?? throw new UnauthorizedAccessException("No sub claim");
    return Guid.Parse(raw);
}
```

Also verify the `type` claim equals `"customer"` (belt-and-braces alongside the policy) and throw `UnauthorizedAccessException` otherwise.

| Method | Route | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/portal/me` | Return `{ id, email, fullName }` for the current customer. |
| `POST` | `/api/portal/tickets` | Create a `Ticket` with `CustomerId = GetActorCustomerId()`. Ignore any `CustomerId` in the body if a client sends one. Set `Status = "Open"`, `CreatedAtUtc = UtcNow`, no assignee. Populate SLA fields identically to `TicketsController.Create` so Story 10 escalation applies unchanged. Return the created ticket. Audit-log. |
| `GET` | `/api/portal/my-requests` | List tickets `WHERE CustomerId == GetActorCustomerId()` ordered by `CreatedAtUtc desc`. |
| `GET` | `/api/portal/my-requests/{id}` | Return detail **only** if `Ticket.CustomerId == GetActorCustomerId()`; else **404** (not 403 — mirrors NotificationsController). Include a read-only history/notes timeline: staff-authored `TicketNote` entries visible to customer + status-change events. **Never expose** internal assignee, agent names, staff notes marked internal, or attachments not authored by this customer. |
| `POST` | `/api/portal/my-requests/{id}/feedback` | 1) 404 if ticket missing or `CustomerId != GetActorCustomerId()`. 2) 400 (or 409) if `Ticket.Status != "Closed"` **exact string match** (Decision 4). 3) 409 if a `TicketFeedback` already exists for this ticket. 4) Validate `Rating in 1..5`, `Comment` length ≤2000. 5) Persist. Audit-log. |

- Ownership check pattern: `_db.Tickets.FirstOrDefaultAsync(t => t.Id == id && t.CustomerId == me)` — a single query that returns null when either the row does not exist or is not the caller's; both branches return the **same 404** so existence is not leaked.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Existing customer with no password logs in** → 401 (`PasswordHash == null`); UI prompts them to register instead. Enforced in `PortalController` login (Task 4).
- **Register collision on an existing customer with a password already set** → 409. Enforced in Task 4.
- **Register on an existing customer with `PasswordHash == null`** → success, updates the same row (do not create a duplicate). Enforced in Task 4.
- **Customer submits a ticket with a `customerId` field in the request body** → the server ignores it and uses the JWT `sub`. Enforced by `PortalController.POST /tickets` never reading a `CustomerId` from input.
- **Customer requests `GET /api/portal/my-requests/{id}` for a ticket that exists but belongs to another customer** → 404, not 403. Enforced by the single-query `WHERE Id == id AND CustomerId == me` pattern (Task 6).
- **Customer submits feedback on a ticket with `Status != "Closed"`** (including `"closed"` lowercase, `"Resolved"`, `"On Hold"`, etc.) → 400/409. Enforced by exact-string check in Task 6, not by casing/normalization.
- **Customer submits a second feedback on the same ticket** → 409 (unique index on `TicketFeedback.TicketId`).
- **Feedback rating out of 1..5 range** → 400.
- **Staff token calls `POST /api/portal/tickets`** → 403 via `RequireCustomer` policy.
- **Customer token calls `GET /api/tickets`, `/api/customers`, `/api/notifications`, `/api/admin/*`, `/api/quick-replies`** → 403 via `RequireStaff` policy on those controllers (Task 3.5).
- **Customer token calls `POST/PUT/DELETE /api/knowledge-articles`** → 403; `GET` is allowed.
- **Unauthenticated call to `POST /api/portal/tickets`** → 401.
- **Empty search string on KB** → return all articles; do not error.
- **Unicode / RTL characters in article `Title`/`Body`** → stored and returned unchanged; search is case-insensitive `Contains`. Do not attempt normalization.
- **Concurrent register on the same email** → the unique index on `Customer.Email` guarantees one wins; the other surfaces a 409 (catch DbUpdateException → conflict).
- **JWT missing the `type` claim (legacy token issued before this story)** → `RequireStaff` and `RequireCustomer` both fail → 403. Users must re-login. Document in migration notes below.
- **Frontend has both staff and customer sessions in localStorage** → each Axios instance reads its own store's token; do not merge. `RequirePortalAuth` never inspects `useAuthStore`, and `RequireAuth` never inspects `useCustomerAuthStore`.

## Test Plan

Unit / integration tests to add under `backend/tests/` (create the test project if not present, else co-locate with existing tests). If no backend test project exists in this repo yet, add these as `.http` requests under `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/CustomerSupportCrm.Api.http` covering the same matrix, mirroring how the current `.http` file exercises staff endpoints.

1. **JwtTokenService** — issuing a token with `identityType = "customer"` emits `type=customer` claim and no role claims; overload for `User` still emits `type=staff` and expected roles.
2. **Policy wiring** — `RequireStaff` rejects a token containing `type=customer`; `RequireCustomer` rejects one containing `type=staff`; both reject a token with no `type` claim.
3. **Customer register** — happy path, collision on email-with-password (409), collision on email-without-password (upgrades row, 200).
4. **Customer login** — happy path, wrong password (401), unknown email (401), email exists with `PasswordHash == null` (401).
5. **KB CRUD as Admin** — list/search/create/get/update/delete all 200.
6. **KB CRUD as Agent** — list/search/create/get/update/delete all 200 (Decision 3).
7. **KB search** — `?q=` matches title and body case-insensitively; empty `q` returns all.
8. **KB write as Customer** — POST/PUT/DELETE all 403; GET list/detail 200.
9. **Portal submit-ticket** — happy path stores `CustomerId = caller`; passing a different `CustomerId` in body is ignored.
10. **Portal my-requests list** — returns only caller's tickets; another customer's tickets not present.
11. **Portal my-request detail** — 200 for own, 404 for other's, 404 for missing (identical response shape — verify byte-for-byte).
12. **Portal feedback** — accepted on `Status="Closed"`, rejected on any other status including `"closed"` lowercase and `"Resolved"`, rejected for non-owner (404), rejected for duplicate submission (409), rejected on rating out of range.
13. **Cross-boundary sweep** — for each of `TicketsController`, `CustomersController`, `NotificationsController`, `AdminController` audit-log endpoint, `QuickRepliesController`: hit one representative endpoint with a customer token → 403.
14. **Cross-boundary sweep, reverse** — for each of `POST /api/portal/tickets`, `GET /api/portal/my-requests`, `GET /api/portal/my-requests/{id}`, `POST /api/portal/my-requests/{id}/feedback`, `GET /api/portal/me`: hit with a staff token → 403.
15. **Regression** — existing staff login still succeeds and returns a working token; existing `[Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]` on user-delete still enforces Admin-only (now via `RequireStaff` + Roles).

Frontend smoke (manual, checklisted):

16. Staff `/knowledge-base` — create, edit, delete, search — English and Arabic.
17. Portal `/portal/register` → `/portal/login` → `/portal/submit` → `/portal/my-requests` → detail → feedback on a Closed ticket — English and Arabic, mobile viewport (≤ 640 px).
18. Reload persistence: staff session survives reload; portal session survives reload; logging out of one does not log out of the other.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Legacy JWTs** issued before this story lack the `type` claim and will be rejected by both policies. Users must re-login. Communicate this in the story's release notes; there is no runtime backfill.
- **Migration `AddKbAndPortal`** is additive (new nullable column, two new tables, one new unique index on `Customer.Email` if not already present). If the email unique index conflict fires on apply, resolve data first (deduplicate customer rows by email) before re-running — do **not** drop the index.
- **Rollback:** revert the migration via `dotnet ef database update <previous>` targeting `AddSlaAndNotifications` (Story 10's migration). Delete new controllers, DTOs, and entities. Restore the original `JwtTokenService.IssueToken(User, …)` signature (or keep the overload — it is source-compatible). Revert `Program.cs` policy registrations. Frontend: delete new files and revert `AppRouter.tsx`/`AppShell.tsx`/`httpClient.ts`.
- **Half-applied risk:** if the migration applies but the code deploy fails, existing staff flow keeps working because `PasswordHash` is nullable and unused on existing endpoints, and the two new tables are simply empty. Safe to roll forward.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** run `dotnet build backend/CustomerSupportCrm.Sln` — must be **0 warnings, 0 errors**.
2. **Migration applies:** `dotnet ef database update --project backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api` — succeeds on a fresh dev DB and on a copy of a Story-10 dev DB.
3. **Backend runs:** `dotnet run --project backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api` — hit `/health` (still `[AllowAnonymous]`, still 200).
4. **API sweep:** run the expanded `CustomerSupportCrm.Api.http` covering test-plan items 3–14.
5. **Frontend builds:** `pnpm --dir frontend build` (or `npm --prefix frontend run build`) — **0 warnings, 0 errors**.
6. **Frontend lint:** `pnpm --dir frontend lint` — clean.
7. **Frontend runs:** `pnpm --dir frontend dev` — visit `/login` (staff) and `/portal/login` (customer), each on its own store; confirm cross-tab persistence.
8. **i18n regression:** toggle to Arabic on both shells — every new string is translated, RTL layout correct on portal shell.
9. **Mobile regression:** DevTools 360 × 640 — Submit Ticket, My Requests, KB pages usable.
10. **Regression:** run through Stories 03/04/05/06/07/08/09/10 happy paths using a staff account — no observable change.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] `Customer` has a nullable `PasswordHash` column; migration applies cleanly.
- [ ] `JwtTokenService` issues tokens with a `type` claim; staff = `"staff"`, customer = `"customer"`.
- [ ] `RequireStaff` and `RequireCustomer` policies are registered in `Program.cs`.
- [ ] Every pre-existing `[Authorize]`-protected staff endpoint uses `RequireStaff` (verified by grep).
- [ ] `POST /api/portal/auth/register` and `POST /api/portal/auth/login` work end-to-end.
- [ ] Admin and Agent can list/search/create/edit/delete KB articles; customers can list/search/get but not write.
- [ ] Customers can submit tickets (server-resolved owner), list/view only their own, and submit feedback **only** on `Status == "Closed"` tickets, once per ticket.
- [ ] All cross-boundary rejections (AC #14, #15, #16) verified with both directions of cross-token tests.
- [ ] Portal has its own login/register/shell/routes; staff and customer sessions coexist in localStorage without collision.
- [ ] All new user-facing strings exist in both `en.json` and `ar.json`; portal renders correctly in RTL and on mobile.
- [ ] Backend and frontend build cleanly (0 warnings/errors); frontend lint passes.
- [ ] Stories 01–10 regression walkthrough passes.
